title: TEACHING ENGLISH ESSAY WRITING USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HIGH SCHOOL
venue: I. Yakovlev Chuvash State Pedagogical University Bulletin
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how to teach English essay writing to secondary school students using artificial intelligence, with a focus on AI-based writing mentors such as ChatGPT. The authors argue that writing is one of the most difficult foreign-language skills to teach because it requires strong control of grammar, vocabulary, spelling, style, logic, and structure, while also placing heavy feedback demands on teachers. They also examine the broader pedagogical question of how AI can be integrated into writing instruction without simply allowing students to outsource authorship.

The study combines several components: a review of writing exercises and AI tools for writing instruction, a survey of 20 foreign-language teachers in Cheboksary about AI use in language teaching, and an experimental classroom trial of the authors’ exercise system for essay writing. The intervention centers on a staged methodology in which students first learn essay structure and argumentation, write an in-class draft independently, then use ChatGPT with a teacher-provided prompt to analyze structure, style, grammar, vocabulary, and argumentation before revising their essays. Students then reflect on the revisions and complete a new in-class essay without AI support. The paper also includes a comparative analysis of several AI writing tools (Kampus AI, WordyBot, Character AI, ChatGPT, DeepSeek), concluding that ChatGPT offers the most detailed and adaptable feedback.

The population studied was high school students, specifically a 10th-grade class at Secondary School No. 65 in Cheboksary, Russia, along with a teacher survey sample of school foreign-language teachers from the same city. The school-based experimental component included both an experimental group and a control group, with writing performance assessed using English Unified State Exam preparation materials and scoring criteria from the Federal Institute of Pedagogical Measurements.

The authors report that the experimental group improved from 3.4 to 4.3 points, while the control group improved from 4.0 to 4.4 points, which they interpret as evidence that AI-supported writing instruction can improve students’ writing skills more than traditional instruction. They conclude that AI-based writing mentors can provide fast personalized feedback, support student independence, reduce anxiety around making mistakes, and save teacher time, but should be used under teacher supervision. For the specific retrieval topic, the paper does mention reduced anxiety and increased independence, and it includes an immediate unaided writing task after AI-supported revision was removed. However, it does not report subgroup or moderator analyses by baseline writing proficiency, English learner status, disability, gender, grade level, school achievement level, subject area, or writing genre; nor does it report delayed follow-up, self-efficacy scales, metacognition measures, authorial voice, plagiarism outcomes, or overreliance effects.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed classroom experiment with a control group, but key credibility elements are missing: sample size is not reported, assignment procedures are unclear, and no inferential statistics or effect sizes are provided. The paper includes some empirical outcome data, but methodological reporting is too limited for green-tier causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported writing gains are directionally positive and larger in the AI-supported group (+0.9 vs. +0.4), suggesting potentially meaningful benefit for secondary EFL writing. However, because no standardized effect size, sample size, or significance testing is reported, impact remains unclear rather than firmly established.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as an AI writing mentor to provide feedback on high-school students’ self-authored English essays, including comments on structure, style, argumentation, grammar, lexis, spelling, and revision recommendations for EFL essay writing.
Conversational chatbot interaction with ChatGPT to guide students through iterative essay revision via prompts, clarifying questions, and personalized feedback during post-draft editing.

finding.finding_summary: In a classroom experiment with 10th-grade students, the experimental group using AI-supported essay revision improved from 3.4 to 4.3 points (+0.9), while the control group improved from 4.0 to 4.4 points (+0.4) on English essay-writing performance using criteria drawn from the Russian Federal Institute of Pedagogical Measurements exam-prep materials. This suggests greater gains in writing performance for the AI-supported group, but the paper does not report sample size, statistical significance tests, or standardized effect sizes, and baseline scores were lower in the experimental group.
finding.measure: Teacher-rated English essay-writing performance using EGE-aligned criteria/materials from the Federal Institute of Pedagogical Measurements

finding.finding_summary: The authors conclude that AI writing mentors reduce students’ anxiety about making mistakes during English essay writing. However, this appears to be based on observational or reflective interpretation from the implementation rather than a validated anxiety scale or reported quantitative comparison.
finding.measure: Perceived student anxiety when making writing errors

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that working with ChatGPT feedback supported students’ independence, self-editing, reflection, and more conscious writing; students revised their own drafts based on AI recommendations and later wrote a new essay without AI support. While this indicates improvement in independent revision and metacognitive writing processes, no subgroup analyses, delayed transfer measures, or validated metacognition/self-efficacy instruments are reported.
finding.measure: Observed/self-reflective development of independence, self-editing, reflection, and unaided writing on a subsequent in-class essay

finding.finding_summary: The authors argue that AI writing mentors provide fast personalized feedback and save teacher time in essay checking and error analysis. This is presented as a practical advantage of the intervention, but no direct timing data, workload logs, or comparative efficiency metrics are reported.
finding.measure: Perceived speed/personalization of feedback and teacher time savings
